weaponsmith.A: Welcome to the forge! If you'd like to turn a bar of metal into a sword worth carrying, I'd be proud to teach you.
weaponsmith.B: Ready to learn weaponsmithing? I'll show you how to make swords, daggers and greataxes at the forge, one good hammer stroke at a time.
weaponsmith.C: You've come to learn weaponsmithing? I'll teach you to make swords at the forge; we'll give all that hammering a point.

armorsmith.A: There's a quiet pride in making armour someone can trust. Join me at the forge, and I'll teach you to make metal armour and shields.
armorsmith.B: Let's put that metal to work. I'll teach you to make armour and shields at the forge, from a sturdy helmet to the boots beneath it.
armorsmith.C: You can make quite an entrance in metal armour, especially on stairs. I'll teach you to make it, and shields, at the forge.

alchemist.A: Curious about Alchemy? You're welcome at the brewing stand, where I'll teach you to bottle a little help for the road in potions and elixirs.
alchemist.B: Let's learn Alchemy: ingredients in, useful potions and elixirs out. I'll show you the recipes at the brewing stand.
alchemist.C: With Alchemy, you can keep a little recovery in your pocket. I'll teach you potions at the brewing stand; do mind the corks.

tailor.A: Ah, you'd like to learn tailoring! Join me at the tailor bench, and we'll make cloth armour, roomy bags and well-bound spellbooks.
tailor.B: You bring the cloth; I'll teach you what to do with it. At the tailor bench, you can make cloth armour, bags and spellbooks.
tailor.C: If your bag is full, I can teach you to make another. Come to the tailor bench for bags, cloth armour and spellbooks; the collecting is up to you.

leatherworker.A: Good leather has many journeys in it. Join me at the tanning rack, and I'll teach you to make leather armour, bags and bows for yours.
leatherworker.B: Ready to learn leatherworking? I'll teach you leather armour, bags and bows at the tanning rack: a useful craft for a long road.
leatherworker.C: You can wear this craft, carry it or draw a bow with it. I'll teach you leather armour, bags and bows at the tanning rack; it's a versatile line of work.

woodcarver.A: Welcome, aspiring woodcarver! Take a place at the carving bench, and I'll teach you to shape wands and staves worthy of your next spell.
woodcarver.B: Want to make your own wands and staves? I'll teach you woodcarving at the carving bench, from the first cut to a finished caster's weapon.
woodcarver.C: You bring the magic; I'll teach you to make something to wave it with. At the carving bench, woodcarving gives you wands and staves.

goldsmith.A: An eye for the finer things? Join me at the jeweller's bench, and I'll teach you goldsmithing: rings, pendants and little treasures with real purpose.
goldsmith.B: Let's give your eye for detail a job. I'll teach you to make rings, amulets and medallions at the jeweller's bench.
goldsmith.C: Good things come in small settings. I'll teach you rings, pendants and medallions at the jeweller's bench; you can supply the admiring glances.

mender.A: Welcome to Grudge-Free Repairs! I'll mend your worn equipment for coin; any grudges it picked up along the way can stay outside.
mender.B: You've reached Grudge-Free Repairs: worn equipment fixed for coin. The work has a price; the lack of hard feelings is on the house.
mender.C: You've found Grudge-Free Repairs! I'll mend your equipment for coin; old grudges are beyond repair, but your boots aren't.
